subject: bumblebee
title: Bumblebees Kept Flying in Air Thinner Than the Top of Everest

scenes.text: People say bumblebees shouldn't be able to fly. Some can fly higher than Everest.
Scientists caught wild bumblebees in China that already live above three thousand metres.
They sealed them in a chamber and slowly pumped out the air.
Every bee could fly at the air of four thousand metres. Two kept hovering past nine thousand.
How? They didn't flap faster. They swept their wings through a wider arc, moving more air each beat.
Mount Everest is eight thousand eight hundred forty-nine metres. So much for not being able to fly.

description:
In a 2014 Biology Letters study, wild alpine bumblebees from China were placed in a chamber where the air was gradually thinned; all could fly at a simulated 4,000 m, and some kept hovering at air density beyond 9,000 m, higher than Everest's summit.
They compensated by sweeping their wings through a wider arc rather than beating faster.
What's the highest place you've ever been?
first_comment: The bees in the test already lived above 3,000 metres. Would you rather have a bee's wings or a bird's lungs?
